newsitem.title: USA: Ford selling Budget to Team Rental for $350 million.
newsitem.headline: Ford selling Budget to Team Rental for $350 million.

text.p: Ford Motor Co. said Tuesday it agreed to sell its Budget Rent a Car Corp. unit to Team Rental Group Inc., its biggest franchisee, for about $350 million.
Budget, together with its independent licensees, is the world's fourth-largest rental car business.
"It's a good fit," Ford Vice Chairman Ed Hagenlocker said in a statement announcing the sale, which had been expected.
Florida-based Team Rental owns and operates 13 Budget franchises with a total of 155 locations. It also leases vans for commuter pooling in 22 states, and markets used vehicles.
Ford said it will continue as a major supplier of cars and trucks to Budget's fleet under a new vehicle supply arrangement that is part of the announced transaction.

Ford, the No.2 U.S. auto maker, also owns Hertz Corp., the nation's largest rental car company, which it acquired in 1994. It said this month that it was reviewing strategic options for Hertz that could include a partial sale.
However, Hagenlocker declined to say Tuesday whether any actions concerning Hertz would occur.
Ford's stock closed Monday at $33.25 on the New York Stock Exchange. Team Rental's stock closed at $23.50.
